# Handover 1.1 — Configuration and root discovery

## What landed

- `5f6d8ad` Add config: defaults, unknown-key check, root discovery
- New package `internal/config`: `Config{Dir, Kinds, Areas}`, `Load(root)`,
  `FindRoot(start)`, `ErrNoRoot`, constants `FileName`, `DefaultDir`, and
  `DefaultKinds`.
- Added `github.com/BurntSushi/toml v1.6.0` (go.mod/go.sum) and updated
  `flake.nix` `vendorHash` to `sha256-n58Qmiv3gik1qkuXQFbQ+soeOQtUz1dUocEAJepqp/E=`.
- Tests cover defaults, a full file, an unknown key, discovery from a nested
  directory, and absence of any file above.

## Landmark drift

None. `docs/DESIGN.md` §2 is unchanged and matches the code.

## Deviations from the work order

- The unit named only `FindRoot`'s signature. I gave `Load(root string)` a
  directory argument (it reads `root/.benchpress.toml`) since callers get the
  root from `FindRoot`; the plan left this open.
- Defaults are decided with `toml.MetaData.IsDefined`: an absent `kinds` gets
  `DefaultKinds`; a `dir` that is absent **or empty** gets `DefaultDir`.
- Unknown-key error wording is mine: `unknown key "foo" in .benchpress.toml`
  (multiple keys are joined). The test asserts only that the key is named.

## What the next session must know

- `FindRoot` returns an absolute path and returns `ErrNoRoot` (usable with
  `errors.Is`) whose message is exactly §2's
  `no .benchpress.toml here or above; run benchpress init`.
- `Load` applies no default to an explicitly empty `kinds = []`; the design is
  silent on that case.
- `Config` fields are exported and untagged beyond the toml names; later units
  (init, board, lint) can build on it. `DefaultKinds` is a package var so
  `init` can serialise it.
- nix sees only tracked files: new files were staged before building. The tree
  is clean; nothing else was touched.

## Open problems

- None blocking. The error-message format for unknown keys is unspecified by
  the design beyond "naming any unknown key", so a later unit that pins a format
  may need to change it.

# Handover 1.2 — Topic files

## What landed

- `96d29de` Add topic: parse front matter, title and links, edit lines
- New package `internal/topic`, pure text over bytes: `Parse`, `Set`, `Remove`,
  `ValidSlug`, `Slugify`, and types `Topic`, `Field`, `Link`, `Issue`.
- `Parse` returns the fields with their lines, the title and its line, every
  relative link with its line, and the structural §6 issues
  (`front-matter`, `unknown-key`, `duplicate-key`, `missing-key`, `title`).
- Tests cover a valid topic, one case per structural issue with its line, links
  inside and outside fences and inline code, `Set` replace/append in LF and CRLF,
  `Remove`, byte preservation (trailing spaces, CRLF, no final newline),
  `ValidSlug` and `Slugify`. `scripts/verify`, `go test ./...` and
  `nix build .#benchpress` are green; no dependency change, `vendorHash` untouched.

## Landmark drift

None. `docs/DESIGN.md` §3 and the `new` row of §7 are as the plan described.

## Deviations from the work order

- The work order fixed the functions, not the `Topic` shape. I chose
  `Fields []Field` in file order plus `Topic.Field(key)`, `Title`/`TitleLine`,
  `Links []Link`, and `Issue{Rule,Line,Message}`.
- `ValidSlug` validates a **file name** including `.md`, matching §3's regex
  literally (`drafts-strand.md` true, `drafts-strand` false). §3 calls the file
  name the slug, but §7's CLI writes `<slug>.md`, so a bare slug is not valid to
  it. A later unit can wrap it if it wants bare-slug checking.
- Missing/unclosed front matter makes `Parse` return early with only that
  `front-matter` issue (no fields, title or links), so a §6 `front-matter`
  fixture yields exactly that one rule.
- `missing-key` issues use line 1 ("no better line" per §6). Issues are sorted
  by line, stably, before returning.
- `Set`/`Remove` return `ErrNoFrontMatter` for a file without a closed front
  matter; `Remove` is a no-op (returns a copy) when the key is absent.

## What the next session must know

- `Topic` carries no slug/path: `board` derives the slug from the file name and
  passes file names to `ValidSlug`.
- `Link.Target` is already cleaned: fragment stripped, and scheme, absolute and
  bare-fragment links are dropped. `linkTarget` also drops a `"title"`.
- Issue messages are freeform; only rule and line are contractual. If 2.3 pins
  wording, change it here.
- Fence handling is deliberately simple: a line with 3+ backticks or tildes
  opens; the matching char closes when the rest is spaces. No nesting-aware
  Markdown parsing.
- `Set` appends with the closing `---`'s terminator, so CRLF files stay CRLF.

## Open problems

- `![alt](img.png)` is treated as a link (the `!` is skipped); the design does
  not say whether images count for the `link`/`topic-link` rules.
- Inline link parsing assumes no nested brackets in the text and no `)` in a
  target/title; it is not a full CommonMark link parser.
- `ValidSlug`'s file-name-vs-bare-slug reading is the main judgement call; 2.3
  or 2.4 will show which the rest of the code needs.

1.3.handover:
# Handover 1.3 — NEXT.md

## What landed

- `a4646ff` Add next: parse NEXT.md items and rewrite the list block
- New package `internal/next`, pure text over bytes: `New`, `Parse`, `Render`,
  and the operations `Add`, `AddAt`, `Remove`, `Move`; types `Next`, `Item`;
  sentinels `ErrPosition`, `ErrNoItem`.
- `Parse` splits every list line (`- ` or `N. ` at column 1) into an `Item`
  with its line, leading-link target and content; non-item lines are kept raw in
  two groups (before and after the first item).
- `Render` numbers the items `1. `.. into one contiguous block where the first
  item stood, keeps every non-item line, and keeps the file's newline style and
  final-newline state. Tests cover mixed bullets/numbers, prose between items,
  no-link items, all four operations and their error cases, a no-item file and
  byte-for-byte round trips (LF, CRLF, no final newline).
- `scripts/verify`, `go test ./...` and `nix build .#benchpress` are green; no
  dependency change, `vendorHash` untouched.

## Landmark drift

None. `docs/DESIGN.md` §4 is as the plan described.

## Deviations from the work order

- The unit fixed `Parse`, `Render` and `New` but not the operations' shapes. I
  chose `Add(Item)` to append, `AddAt(Item, at)` for a 1-based insert (end is
  `len+1`), and target-based `Remove(target)` / `Move(target, at)`. Out-of-range
  positions wrap `ErrPosition`; an absent target wraps `ErrNoItem`.
- `Item.Text` is the whole item content **without** its marker (the `- `/`N. `),
  so rendering is `strconv.Itoa(n) + ". " + Text`. Target is the leading link's
  relative target, mirroring `topic.cleanTarget`: fragment stripped, and empty
  for schemes, absolute paths, bare fragments and non-links.
- `Item.Line` is the source line for parsed items, 0 for added ones; it is not
  used by `Render`.
- The HEAD/TAIL split is a rendering device, not part of the public API: only
  `Items` and the operations are exported.

## What the next session must know

- `Move`/`Remove` identify an item by `Target`. Items with no link (`Target ==
  ""`) cannot be moved or removed this way; board `J`/`K` should read
  `Items[pos].Target` first, or a positional operation can be added.
- Duplicate targets are not prevented here (that is lint's `next-duplicate`);
  target-based ops act on the first match.
- Rendering normalises terminators to the file's dominant style (`\n` or
  `\r\n` detected from the first newline). A file with mixed terminators will
  not round-trip byte for byte; uniform files do.
- `Add` does not check for a duplicate target.

## Open problems

- The unit's phrase "the text after the link" could be read as a separate
  suffix field; I read it as the item content minus marker, since the link's
  display text must survive for a faithful rewrite. If 2.3/2.4 want the suffix
  only, add a field here.
- No markdown fence handling: a `- ` line inside a fenced code block counts as
  an item. §4 gives no fence exception, unlike §3 for topics.

2.1.handover:
# Handover 2.1 — Where plans are

## What landed

- `d537e8f` Add repo: locate paths in the worktree and local branches
- New package `internal/repo`, read-only git. `New(root)` returns `*Repo`;
  `Find(ctx, paths...) (map[string][]string, error)` returns, per path, the
  ordered places holding it: `repo.Worktree` ("worktree") first when it exists
  on disk, then each local branch short name that holds it.
- `Locator` interface (`Find(ctx, paths...) (map[string][]string, error)`) is
  defined in `repo` and satisfied by `*Repo`; lint/board can hold it and fake it
  without git.
- Per §5: one `git for-each-ref --format=%(refname:short) refs/heads`, then one
  `git ls-tree -r --name-only <branch> -- <path>...` per branch, all paths at
  once. No other git command is run. Tests record the subcommands to prove it.
- Outside a repository, `for-each-ref` fails and `Find` returns the worktree
  hits with a nil error.
- `scripts/verify`, `go test ./...` and `nix build .#benchpress` green. No
  `go.mod`/`go.sum` change; `vendorHash` untouched.

## Landmark drift

None. §5 read as written. `internal/lint` does not exist yet, so the interface
could not be defined in it; see deviations.

## Deviations from the work order

- The unit let the interface live "here or in `lint`". `lint` does not exist
  yet, so I defined `repo.Locator` in `repo`. 2.3's lint can take `repo.Locator`
  directly; if it prefers its own interface, define it there and drop this one
  instead of duplicating.
- `Find` takes a `context.Context` and returns an error (git can fail per
  branch), rather than a bare map. Outside a repo the error is nil.
- Results are a map from path to a slice of locations, not one call per path:
  §5's whole point is batching every plan path into the per-branch `ls-tree`.

## What the next session must know

- Locations are repo-root-relative strings; "worktree" is `repo.Worktree`.
  Branch order is for-each-ref's, i.e. refname-sorted.
- `Find` swallows *any* `for-each-ref` error as "not a repository" (no
  `rev-parse` is run, per the command restriction). A `ls-tree` error on a real
  branch is returned.
- Paths are matched literally against `ls-tree` output; a path is expected to be
  a file, not a directory or glob. No `:(literal)` pathspec is used.
- Tests live in `package repo` and set `HOME` via `t.Setenv`, plus
  `GIT_CEILING_DIRECTORIES` in the non-repo test so a parent repo cannot leak in.
  Repo tests use `git init -b main` for a deterministic base branch.

## Open problems

- `for-each-ref` failure being treated as non-repo can hide a broken git; no
  distinction is possible without a third command, which the done-when forbids.
- For a very large path set the `ls-tree` argument list is unbounded; fine for
  plan paths, worth revisiting only if callers batch wildly.

# Handover 2.2 — Loading the board, and `ls`

## What landed

- `5261897` Add board: load topics and Next, and the ls command
- New package `internal/board`: `Load(root, cfg) (*Board, error)` reads every
  `*.md` directly in `cfg.Dir` except `NEXT.md` and `README.md`, parses each with
  `topic.Parse`, and parses `NEXT.md` with `next.Parse`. `Topic` holds Slug,
  repo-relative Path, `Parsed topic.Topic` and structural `Issues`, with
  `Kind/Area/State/Plan/Title/Broken/FirstIssue` accessors.
- `Board.Listing(Filter, planFound)` returns the `next` slugs and the ordered
  `[]Entry`, and `Board.Plans()` the distinct plan paths of planned topics.
  Ordering: Next items in Next order, then other topics by configured area
  order (then alphabetical, then no area last), state `open`,`settled`,`planned`,
  then title, then slug.
- `benchpress ls` (new `cmd/benchpress/ls.go`), with repeatable `--state`,
  `--kind`, `--area` and `--json`. Plan locations come from `repo.Find` over
  `Board.Plans()`. `main.go` now exposes `newRootCmd()` so the command is
  testable.
- Tests: `internal/board/board_test.go` on `t.TempDir()` fixtures (ordering,
  ignored README/non-md/subdirs, broken topic, filters, plan locations,
  alphabetical areas, missing dir); `cmd/benchpress/ls_test.go` runs `ls` and
  `ls --json` in a fixture and checks text order and JSON.
- `scripts/verify`, `go test ./...`, `nix build .#benchpress` green. No
  `go.mod`/`go.sum` change; `vendorHash` untouched.

## Landmark drift

None. `docs/DESIGN.md` §2 and the `ls` row of §7 are as the plan described.
`internal/lint` still does not exist, so `ls` uses `repo.New` directly.

## Deviations from the work order

- §7 does not fix the text format, only the fields. I chose group headings
  (`Next`, then each area name), each topic line indented two spaces:
  `slug  state  kind  title`, plus `  plan (worktree, branch…)` for a planned
  topic (`(not found)` when nowhere). A broken topic's line is
  `slug  <first issue message>`.
- Filters apply to the whole view: a Next item filtered out is omitted from
  both the `next` array and the groups. The design is silent; this matches
  "filter".
- `next` and `topics` in `--json` are always `[]`/arrays, never `null`;
  `plan_found` is `[]` for topics with no plan.
- A missing workbench `dir` yields an empty board rather than an error (the
  design is silent; §2 only fails on a missing `.benchpress.toml`).

## What the next session must know

- `Board.Topics` is sorted by slug and carries the raw `topic.Topic` (Fields,
  Links, TitleLine) and `Issues`; lint 2.3 can build its rules from it plus
  `Board.Next` and `Board.Config`. `lint` can take `repo.Locator` for plans.
- `Entry.Issue` holds the first structural issue; `Entry.Broken()` is
  `Issue != nil`. `Entry.PlanFound` is filled only for `state: planned` with a
  plan, from the map passed to `Listing`.
- `targetSlug` matches a Next link target to a slug by base name (`a/b.md` →
  `b`); a Next item whose target names no loaded topic is skipped by `ls`
  (that is lint's `next-item`).
- The command test chdirs into the fixture and sets `HOME` and
  `GIT_CEILING_DIRECTORIES`; do not run such tests in parallel.

## Open problems

- A broken topic's parse error is shown in the text but **not** in `--json`:
  §7's JSON schema has no error field, and I did not add one. If 2.3/2.4 fix a
  wording or want the error in JSON, that schema must change in `docs/DESIGN.md`.
- `ls` treats any structural issue as "broken" and prints only slug+error,
  dropping a partially parsed state/kind/title. This is my reading of "listed by
  slug with its parse error".
- Group headings and the two-space indent are invented (see deviations); a
  later unit pinning ls's exact text must revisit them.

2.3.handover:
# Handover 2.3 — Lint

## What landed

- New package `internal/lint`: `Check(ctx, *board.Board, repo.Locator) ([]Problem, error)`.
  `Problem{Path, Line, Severity, Rule, Message}` carries the rule name, so
  `--json` and tests both see it. It maps `board.Topic.Issues` (topic's own
  structural rules) plus the value, Next and link rules of §6, sorts by path
  then line, and returns nil when clean. It never prints.
- `benchpress lint [--json]` (`cmd/benchpress/lint.go`): text is
  `path:line: severity: message`, JSON is `{"problems":[…]}`; exits 1 when any
  severity is `error`, 0 otherwise. `main.go` gains `exitError int`, recognized
  by `main`, so a lint failure exits quietly with 1.
- `topic.LineLinks(line, n) []Link` is a new exported wrapper over the existing
  link scanner, so Next item text is scanned with the same parser as topic
  bodies (see deviations).
- Tests: `internal/lint/lint_test.go` has one case per §6 rule name (17 of
  them), each on a minimal fixture producing exactly that rule, plus a clean
  fixture; `cmd/benchpress/lint_test.go` runs the command and checks the path/line
  order, exit 1 on errors, exit 0 on a warning only, and the `--json` shape.
- `scripts/verify`, `go test ./...`, `nix build .#benchpress` green. No
  `go.mod`/`go.sum` change; `vendorHash` untouched.

## Landmark drift

None. `internal/lint` was absent as the plan said; `board.Board`/`board.Topic`,
`repo.Locator`, `config.Config` and `topic` are all where 2.2's handover said.

## Deviations from the work order

- **Next links.** §6's `topic-link` says "from a topic or from Next". `next`
  only exposes an item's leading target, and `topic.collectLinks` was
  unexported, so I added `topic.LineLinks` and scan the whole item text. A Next
  item that begins with a link to a missing `*.md` in `dir` therefore reports
  **both** `next-item` and `topic-link` — two genuinely different problems. The
  minimal-fixture tests keep each rule alone.
- **`link` vs `topic-link` partition.** A relative link resolving under `dir`
  whose target ends `.md` is `topic-link` (error) when missing; a link
  resolving outside `dir` is the `link` warning when missing. Non-`.md` links
  directly in `dir`, and `.md` links under a subdirectory that exist, report
  nothing; §6 does not cover them.
- **`plan` emptiness.** A present-but-empty `plan` counts as no plan: planned →
  `plan-missing`, non-planned → nothing. Only a non-empty plan triggers
  `plan-unexpected`/`plan-gone`.
- **Command exit.** Added `exitError` in `main.go`; the loop's checks read
  `cmd.Execute()`'s error, so this is the testable way to signal exit 1 without
  the process exiting or printing `benchpress:`.

## What the next session must know

- `lint.Check` needs a non-nil `repo.Locator`. It asks it once for `Board.Plans()`;
  with no planned topics it never calls git, so command tests need no repository.
- The plan's JSON `problems` is always an array (`[]` when clean). Messages are
  not pinned by §6; only `rule` is.
- `topic.LineLinks` shares `collectLinks`, so Next link detection matches topic
  bodies exactly (code spans ignored, fragments/schemes/absolute targets dropped).
- 2.4's mutations should run `lint.Check` (or shell `benchpress lint`) after
  writing, per §9; `Check` itself does no writes.

## Open problems

- The two-problems case above is a reading of §6, not stated in the design. If
  the author wants one problem per missing Next target, `checkNext` must skip
  `checkLink` for a leading target that already failed `next-item`.
- §10 calls `lint` a pure package tested on in-memory values, but link
  existence needs the working tree; lint stats `Root` and its tests use
  `t.TempDir`. A future pass may want the file set passed in.
- `ls`'s JSON still has no parse-error field (2.2's open problem); untouched here.

commits: 3c5f119c865c291ebdf1d59bcaa7436d37f3a23d Add the workbench-changing commands and their board operations
2.4.handover:
# Handover 2.4 — Changing the workbench from the command line

## What landed

- `3c5f119` Add the workbench-changing commands and their board operations
- `internal/board/edit.go`: `(*Board).New(title, kind, area, toNext) (string, error)`,
  `SetState(slug, state, plan)`, `NextAdd(slug, at)`, `NextRemove(slug)`,
  `NextMove(slug, at)`, `Remove(slug) ([]string, error)`. `New` builds the file
  (state `open`, `# Title`, empty `**Now:**`/`**Open:**`), validates kind/area
  against `board.Config`, fails on an existing file, a disallowed kind/area and a
  title that makes no slug. `SetState` edits only the `state`/`plan` lines via
  `topic.Set`/`topic.Remove`; `Next*` rewrite Next via `next`'s operations and
  `Render`. All writes go through one `writeAtomic` (temp file in the same dir,
  rename, destination mode kept); `New` also `MkdirAll`s the workbench dir.
- `cmd/benchpress`: `new`, `state`, `next add|rm|mv`, `rm`, wired in `main.go`.
  `new` requires `--kind` and `--area` (cobra `MarkFlagRequired`). `rm` prints the
  linking topics one path per line; every other changing command prints nothing.
- Tests: `internal/board/edit_test.go` on `t.TempDir()` for every operation's
  success and failure (existing file, disallowed kind/area, empty slug, unknown
  slug, `planned` without a plan, bad state, position out of range, already/not
  in Next); `cmd/benchpress/change_test.go` drives the commands and a
  `TestLintCleanAfterChanges` runs all six operations, running `benchpress lint`
  after each and requiring empty output.
- `scripts/verify`, `go test ./...` and `nix build .#benchpress` green. No
  `go.mod`/`go.sum` change; `vendorHash` untouched.

## Landmark drift

None. `topic.Set`/`topic.Remove` and the `next` operations are where 1.2/1.3 left
them; `board.Load`, `repo.Locator`, `config.Config` and `main.go`'s `newRootCmd`
are where 2.2/2.3 left them.

## Deviations from the work order

- **`next add` on an item already in Next is an error.** §4 says a topic appears
  at most once, so the operation refuses to create a duplicate (which would be a
  `next-duplicate` lint error) rather than silently adding one.
- **`state` rejects a value outside `open`/`settled`/`planned`**, and `new`
  rejects a title that slugifies to nothing; neither is spelled out by §7, but
  both would otherwise write an invalid topic.
- **`--at` for `next add` is an `int` flag defaulting to 0, meaning append.**
  An explicit `--at 0` therefore appends rather than erroring.
- **`new` prints the repository-relative path** (e.g. `work/foo.md`), matching
  `ls`'s path style; `rm` prints the linking topics as repository-relative paths.
- **`Remove` deletes the file before rewriting Next**, following §7's wording.
  A failure between the two leaves the item pointing at a missing file; the
  order could be swapped if that partial state is judged worse.

## What the next session must know

- Commands call `loadBoard()` (from `ls.go`), which finds the root and loads
  topic + Next. Mutation methods are on the loaded `*Board`; they do not reload
  it, so a command performs exactly one operation per invocation.
- `requireTopic`/`nextIndex` accept a trailing `.md`, so `<slug>` and `<slug>.md`
  both work. Slugs in `Board.Topics` are bare.
- `linkedBy` resolves a link with `path.Clean(path.Join(cfg.Dir, target))` and
  compares to the topic's `Path`, the same resolution lint uses; self-links are
  skipped. Next items are not scanned (the design says "topics").
- The lint-clean test relies on the fixture's `NEXT.md`, so no `next-absent`
  warning; there are no planned topics, so `lint` never calls git.
- 3.2's board keys should call these same methods (`n` = add-or-remove, `J`/`K` =
  move, `s` = SetState, `a` = New, `d` = Remove) and then reload + re-lint.

## Open problems

- `new` does not escape Markdown in the title, so a title containing `]` or `(`
  makes a Next link that will not parse; §7 is silent and titles are usually
  plain. Consider escaping or validating the title if it matters.
- `New ... toNext` writes the topic, then Next; a failed Next write leaves the
  topic created. No cross-file transaction exists anywhere in this unit.
- `Remove`'s design order (file, then Next) can leave a dangling `next-item` on
  a mid-operation failure; see deviations.
